note: USFS, Hoosier NF. Small primitive campground on a clifftop above the Ohio River, with a short trail to an overlook; tables and grills. --Claude
summary: $0, FCFS always, 5 sites, vault toilet and no water all confirmed. Year-round and 14-night limit added. Site dimensions added: the 'sites are short' note was wrong (50-57 ft paved spurs), dropped. Not waterfront stands; river-view re-audit lead.
flags: PHONE missing: Tell City Ranger District 812-547-7051 (recreation.gov, Google). apply.py doesn't write phone.

FIT: the note's 'Sites are short — verify length' is contradicted: Forest Service gives 12 x 50 to 12 x 57 ft, recreation.gov paved back-ins permitting RV and Trailer with Site Access Drive-In, Driveway Grade 'Slight' on site 2. inclusion_evidence's 'max RV length 30 ft' is allstays; no agency page says it (site 1's Max Vehicle Length reads 0, i.e. blank). A Google reviewer, 3 years ago: 'Could easily fit my truck and cargo trailer. The end of the road is a loop, so you don't have to worry about getting stuck.' Another, a year ago: 'small, sloping spurs, only five sites that are often already taken.' Another, 2 years ago: 'five paved and mostly level back-in sites'. Google 4.5/42. Sound for a 23-ft rig on what is posted.

TOILET conflict: Forest Service page says both 'a portable toilet' and 'no toilets or water are provided'; recreation.gov's newer text says vault toilet, and reviews 2-3 years old describe a clean vault/pit toilet by the sites. Imagery shows a small white structure at the loop. Kept vault_toilets true on recreation.gov.

WATER LEAD: plotted the sites on leaf-off imagery: the nearest, site 4, is about 165 m from the Ohio River in a straight line, down a bluff (stored elevation 199 m). Forest Service: 'Benches are located on the bluffs overlooking the Ohio River'; recreation.gov: 'scenic overlook platform with views of the Ohio River and Kentucky'; a reviewer reaches 'the little overlook' by 'a brief walk down the trail past the bench'. The view belongs to the overlook, not plainly to the pads, which sit in woods; at most a leaf-off '*view' question. Old note said 'river view'; waterfront left as stored, for re-audit. Barge and UPS aircraft noise reported (1 year ago): 'lots of barge traffic with chugging engines and blaring horns'.

ACCESS: a Google review 3 months ago: 'The drive due to construction & my arrival after dark was treacherous!' No agency page or active alert mentions road work, and none describes the approach road (Buzzards Roost Access Rd); the spur on imagery runs in through pines from the north. Couldn't verify grade or width. A 6-months-old review also: 'Grass was overgrown'. Pin sits on the loop, within about 40 m of the sites: no move.
